title: Spinal ligaments
summary: Pull each lumbar and thoracic ligament (bone-ligament-bone) to failure and report stiffness, failure force, elongation, stress, strain and force-deformation points.
simulate: Model each ligament between its bony attachments with in situ length and cross-section (lumbar or thoracic, level as given).
Fix one bone; pull the other along the ligament fibre direction (quasi-static, about 1-10 mm/min or as stated).
Load to failure; record force vs grip deformation from the unloaded (zero-force) length.
Report linear-region stiffness, failure force and elongation, failure stress (force / CSA) and strain (elongation / length).
For curves, report force at the given deformation; for prestrain, the strain of the in situ length relative to the free length.

notes: Stiffness is the linear-region slope; Chazal and Wolny values are derived from characteristic points (note "derived"). Chazal ISL+SSL mixes cadaveric and surgical specimens; Iida (degenerative surgery) is kept separate.

Pintar per-level values (Table 2: stiffness, failure stress/strain, energy for T12-L1..L5-S1), the T12-L2 and L4-S1 curves, Wolny Th1-Th6/Th7-Th12 subgroups and transition points, Wiczenbach points I/II and geometry are in bench/tests, not shown. Pintar n per ligament/level is not reported (n = null).

Left out: Chazal intertransverse ligament (n=2) and pooled C2-S1 points; Neumann marker-based strains/moduli; Tkaczuk yield loads; Little dynamic/viscous moduli and perpendicular curves; Nachemson resting force; Robertson bone/transverse prestrain and 444 N change.
agent_prompt: You are given a model of the human lumbar and thoracic spinal ligaments (ALL, PLL, ligamentum flavum, interspinous, supraspinous, ISL+SSL complex, facet capsule). For every task, isolate the named ligament at the stated level with its bony attachments, apply uniaxial tension along the fibres from the zero-force length (quasi-static) up to failure, or the stated flexion or strain, and report the requested output: linear-region stiffness, failure force, failure elongation, failure stress (force / cross-section), failure strain (elongation / initial length, %), force at the given deformation, stress at the given strain, or in situ prestrain. Keep one parameter set per ligament and level. Return one JSON object following answer_format (task id -> {output key: value}); use null when a task cannot be simulated.
